scenes.vo: A hot dog and a soda at Costco costs one dollar fifty. It has cost one dollar fifty since 1985.
scenes.subtitle: COSTCO · FOOD COURT

scenes.vo: If that price had kept pace with inflation, it would be close to four fifty today.
scenes.title: Hot dog + soda

scenes.vo: So here is the question. Why would a company that watches every penny leave money on the table?
scenes.text: Why won't Costco raise the hot dog?

scenes.vo: Costco opened its first warehouse in Seattle in nineteen eighty three.
scenes.title: Where it started

scenes.vo: Last year it sold almost three hundred billion dollars of goods, at a margin around eleven percent.
scenes.subtitle: COSTCO · FY2026
scenes.source: Costco FY2026 10-K · Net sales, operating income

scenes.vo: The hidden line item is the membership fee. Five point nine billion dollars, about half of operating income.
scenes.label: MEMBERSHIP FEES

scenes.vo: And ninety-two percent of members in the US and Canada renew every year.
scenes.label: of US & Canada members renew

scenes.vo: Here is a number you will not find in the annual report. Lose two points of renewals, and within five years fee revenue falls by about four hundred sixty million dollars. Lose four points, and it is closer to nine hundred million.
scenes.title: If the renewal rate slips

scenes.vo: The hot dog isn't a product. It's the reason you keep paying.
